base-model.t: **Parameters** (left) are learned from the training data. **Hyperparameters** (right) are chosen by us and set outside the fitting, like maximum depth or learning rate.

hyperparameter.t: We will tune **max_depth**: how many questions in a row the tree may ask. We will try the values **1, 2, 4 and 8** and compare the results.

candidate-a.t: The first candidate has depth **1**: a single question. Each candidate gets its own column so the settings can be compared side by side.

candidate-b.t: The second candidate has depth **2**: two questions in a row. It is the same kind of model with a different value of the hyperparameter.

candidate-c.t: The third candidate has depth **4**: four questions in a row, a moderate amount of flexibility.

candidate-d.t: The fourth candidate has depth **8**: very flexible. With all four columns in place the experiment is set up, but nothing has been trained yet.

train-each.t: Each depth is trained on the **training data only**. The small grey figures are training F1 scores, which keep rising with depth. They are **not** what we select on.

validation-results.t: Now each trained model is scored on the **validation data**: **0.46, 0.58, 0.676 and 0.59**. The best score is in the middle, not at the most flexible setting.

select-setting.t: **Depth 4** has the best validation F1 and is highlighted. Choosing by training score would wrongly pick **depth 8**, the overfitted model.

test-stays-locked.t: The test set played **no part** in choosing the depth. **Remember:** tune hyperparameters on validation data, and keep the test set locked until the model and settings are final.
